answer: Draw the auditor at random and weight its verdict by how different its route to the answer was: tools, data source, execution order. Two agents that took the same path cancel out, so cloning a pipeline buys nothing, and nobody audits a recruit they signed. A sybil cluster then has to run genuinely distinct stacks per identity, which costs more than the rewards it chases. The bill: a separate stack, separate data and a separate history per account, paid up front. An orchard of clones needs an orchard of real setups, and no nebula of accounts gets to hide behind a lotus of shared tooling.
